print_orientation: vertical, dispense end (Z=0) on the build plate

pauses.name: Solenoid insertion
pauses.part: Adafruit #412 JF-0530B 5 V mini push-pull solenoid (9.6 × 19 × 22 mm)
pauses.instructions: Pause printer at this Z. v3 places the solenoid LOW (z_center = 15 mm) with the plunger axis along X — i.e. the 22 mm dimension is the radial direction toward the auger bore, matching the through-bore tap slot. Insert the JF-0530B body into the -X pocket (plunger facing +X toward the bore through the 6 × 2.5 mm slot). Route leads through the short radial 2.5 × 3 mm wire-egress slot out the -X face. Resume to lock the solenoid in place.

pauses.name: ERM disc insertion
pauses.part: Adafruit #1201 vibrating motor disc (Ø10 × 2.7 mm, 3 V)
pauses.instructions: Pause printer at this Z. The +X radial pocket (Ø10.3 × 2.9 mm) is open along with the short Ø2.5 × 2 mm radial wire-egress slot directly out the +X face. Epoxy the ERM coin in with leads exiting through the egress slot. Route leads down/around to the e-bay grommet (z = ~152 mm on the +X external wall of the e-bay). Resume to encapsulate the disc.

install_after_print.name: Heat-set inserts
install_after_print.instructions: Press heat-set brass inserts: 4× M3 (Ø4.0 × 5.5 mm deep) into the e-bay lid corner holes (now 6 mm in from each outer edge, well inside the 8.5 mm flange that surrounds the lid opening); 4× M3 into the new servo bracket flange on the +Y face; 4× M2.5 (Ø3.6 × 4.5 mm) into the stepper top plate (23 × 23 mm pattern); 4× M2.5 into the Pi standoffs on the +Y inner wall of the e-bay.

install_after_print.name: Servo external bracket install (v3)
install_after_print.instructions: v3 puts the servo OUTSIDE the chassis on a bracket flange. (a) Slide the servo horn's output spline into the Ø8 mm horn-axle pass-through on the +Y face at z = 50; the rear of the horn shaft is caught by the Ø3.2 × 4 mm bushing socket on the -Y face for both-sided support. (b) Seat the servo case against the Ø16 mm airgap standoff ring on +Y (servo body sits 2 mm proud of the chassis face — leaves a thermal airflow gap; the two ventilation slots at ±26 mm on either side of the horn axle complete the airflow path). (c) Bolt the servo case to the 4 M3 heat-set inserts in the bracket flange. Connect horn linkage to the dispense-end mechanism that the servo is intended to drive (e.g. a dispense gate or rocker tap).

install_after_print.name: Pi Zero 2 W mount
install_after_print.part: Pi Zero 2 W on the +Y inner wall of the e-bay
install_after_print.instructions: Bolt the Pi Zero 2 W flat onto the 4 standoffs on the +Y inner wall of the bay (58 × 23 mm pattern, M2.5 into heat-sets). Orient the board so the mini-HDMI / micro-USB OTG / micro-USB power connector edge faces the -Z bay-floor cable slot (cables exit downward toward the desk).

install_after_print.name: Adafruit Stepper Bonnet stack
install_after_print.part: Adafruit Stepper Motor Bonnet (~65 × 30 × 15 mm) on Pi GPIO
install_after_print.instructions: Press the Bonnet onto the Pi GPIO 2 × 20 header. Bonnet drives the servo (PWM) and solenoid (MOSFET, optionally via a logic-level shifter). The Bonnet's onboard stepper driver is unused for the auger drive in v3 (see Tic 500 entry).

install_after_print.name: Pololu Tic 500 stepper controller (v3: USB-only, no GPIO clash)
install_after_print.instructions: v3 explicitly avoids the Bonnet GPIO contention reported in the v2 Edison review. VHB-tape (3M VHB 5952) the Tic 500 flat against the -X internal sidewall of the e-bay with its micro-USB port facing -Z (toward the bay floor cable slot). The Tic 500 talks to the Pi via micro-USB only — it does not sit on the GPIO header, so the Bonnet has the GPIO to itself. Stepper leads enter the bay through the +X wall grommet at z = 152 mm and land directly on the Tic 500 screw terminals.

install_after_print.name: DRV8825 stepper driver carrier (alternate)
install_after_print.instructions: VHB-tape the DRV8825 onto the +X internal sidewall of the e-bay. Optional fallback driver if not using the Tic 500 — wire to the Bonnet's STEP/DIR breakout pins.

install_after_print.name: E-bay lid
install_after_print.instructions: Print the matching lid (70 × 80 × 2.5 mm with 4 M3 clearance holes at the corners) separately and bolt to the heat-set inserts. v3 lid opening is now 53 × 63 mm (smaller than v2) so the 8.5 mm flange comfortably accommodates the corner inserts.

install_after_print.name: Stepper + coupler install (top, v3)
install_after_print.instructions: v3 fixes the spindle gap: the auger now extends with a Ø5 × 24 mm spindle reaching up from z=250 into the coupler region. The chassis has a Ø6 mm spindle pass-through (z = 250–258) below the full Ø19 coupler chamber. (1) Drop the auger in from above so its spindle pokes through the spindle pass-through into the open coupler chamber. (2) Slide the ST-FC01 coupler into the chamber from above; the auger spindle enters one side. (3) Drop the stepper's Ø5 D-cut shaft into the other side of the coupler. (4) Tighten the two coupler grub screws via the two Ø3.5 mm access ports on the +X face (these line up with the ST-FC01 set screws). (5) Bolt the stepper to the top plate with 4 × M2.5 into the heat-set inserts (23 × 23 mm pattern, Ø22 pilot pass-through). (6) Route the 4 stepper leads down the +X vertical wire slot and into the e-bay through the Ø5 grommet on the +X external wall of the e-bay at z = 152 mm. (v2 had this grommet on the -Y shared wall and only 3.5 mm deep — wires couldn't reach. v3 puts it through the 2.5 mm e-bay outer wall directly into the cavity.)

wiring.summary: All four electrical leads (ERM, solenoid, servo, stepper) terminate inside the -Y e-bay. Servo + solenoid land on the Bonnet (PWM/MOSFET). Stepper lands on the Tic 500 (USB-connected, no GPIO clash).

paths.via: Short +X radial egress slot → down chassis +X face → into e-bay through +X grommet or main lid opening
paths.to: Bonnet PWM output (3 V via logic-level)

paths.via: Short -X radial egress slot → around bottom of chassis → into e-bay lid opening
Around top of chassis → over the airgap ring → into e-bay lid opening
Down the +X vertical wire slot → through the Ø5 grommet on +X e-bay external wall at z=152 → directly to the Tic 500 screw terminals
paths.to: Tic 500 A1/A2/B1/B2 (USB-connected to Pi, no GPIO clash with Bonnet)

bore_breach_zones.summary: v3 separates the two bore-breaching slots so they no longer share any Z range (v2 had a Z=27–29 mm overlap that risked simultaneous powder leak through both sides).

v3_changes: Auger ↔ coupler spindle gap fixed: auger now extends with Ø5 × 24 mm spindle (auger script). Chassis has Ø6 mm pass-through (z=250–258) below the Ø19 coupler chamber.

Servo no longer embedded in a PLA tomb. External bracket on +Y with airgap standoff ring (2 mm), 2 ventilation slots, 4 M3 heat-sets, Ø8 mm horn-axle pass-through, and a Ø3.2 mm rear bushing socket on -Y for both-sided horn support.
E-bay lid heat-set holes moved to a thicker flange (lid opening shrunk from 63 × 75 to 53 × 63; flange grew from 3.5 mm to 8.5 mm).
Solenoid pocket rotated 90° so the 22 mm plunger axis is now along X (radial toward the bore), matching the tap-slot direction.
Stepper wire grommet relocated to the e-bay +X external wall (drilled through 2.5 mm of e-bay wall only) so the wires actually reach the Tic 500.
Solenoid bore-breach moved to z=10–20; servo horn axle at z=46–54. No overlap (25.9 mm clear gap).
Tic 500 GPIO clash with the Bonnet resolved by routing the Tic 500 over USB only (micro-USB port facing the bay floor cable slot).
notes: Pause Z is in millimetres along the chassis Z axis (matches the CadQuery script). Layer index = round(z_mm / layer_height_mm) at 0.2 mm; rescale if you slice differently. The user has chosen to leave the auger as a rotating-as-one-body design (no internal helix actually metering powder); this is acknowledged as a non-functional auger in the geometric sense but is preferred over PLA-on-PLA rubbing. Auger height (auger_tube_length) remains the single parameter to adjust for build-plate Z limits (e.g. shorter on smaller printers; the H2D the user is targeting has plenty of Z).
